title: Bissell Park multi-use pad consulting contract awarded
subtitle: Land purchase beside the Sportsplex, diversity recognition program, SCADA vendor, asset management policy and part lot control exemption.
overview: Council awarded the Bissell Park multi-use surface consulting contract to ATA Architects Inc. for $89,670, excluding HST {{vote:m8}}. The work will study options for replacing the aging pad in Elora, including costs, site limits and operating impacts. Staff expect to report back around the end of August or early September, ahead of 2025 budget talks. Several councillors worried about the cost and the path toward a refrigerated rink.

After a closed session, the Mayor announced the Township bought about 90 acres next to the Centre Wellington Community Sportsplex in Fergus at 8055 Wellington Road 18, for $4.8 million. Council authorized a media release {{vote:m3}}. The land is meant for future parkland and recreation space, and the Parks and Recreation Master Plan is under way.

Council also directed staff to work with the Diversity Equity and Inclusion Advisory Committee on a recognition program, with costs to return in 2025 budget deliberations {{vote:m5}}. It named Eramosa Engineering vendor of record for water and wastewater SCADA services {{vote:m6}}, and adopted an updated Strategic Asset Management Policy {{vote:m9}}.

decisions.detail: Council awarded RFP #06-24 to ATA Architects Inc. at $89,670 excluding HST to assess options and prepare technical studies for the Bissell Park multi-use surface {{vote:m8}}.
Council authorized staff to release details of the acquisition of 8055 Wellington Road 18 in a media release {{vote:m3}}.
Staff will work with the advisory committee to develop a recognition program and return with costs during 2025 budget deliberations.
Eramosa Engineering was established as vendor of record for SCADA, instrumentation and monitoring support for water and wastewater services.
Council adopted the updated policy by by-law and repealed By-law 2019-31.
Consent items were approved, including a part lot control exemption for Lots 80-81 and Blocks 82-84 of Plan 61M-235.

debate: A delegate urged council to stop the refrigerated rink process, citing high capital and operating costs and energy use in other municipalities. The delegate also asked that basketball and other recreational users be treated equitably.

A delegate for the project's founding groups said the pad was always meant to be multi-use. They said refrigeration was undecided, the current surface is deteriorating, and the study would show whether the project is affordable.

Some councillors worried the four options all assume a costly refrigerated pad, and wanted a cheaper option and the Parks and Recreation Master Plan to guide location. Others said the study was needed to know the true costs and phasing.

Staff said the process followed earlier council direction for a refrigerated pad. They said the pad could be built in phases, only one proposal was received, and adding a new option would need negotiation with the vendor. Basketball groups would be added to consultations.
Councillors asked about the funding source and whether the Jack MacDonald funds should pay for studies. Staff said another funding source would need council direction.
